Ben — thanks for the demo last week. Legal has reviewed the order form and asked for a clearer security exhibit before we can route to procurement. High level asks: 

1) SOC 2: we need a copy of the most recent SOC 2 report and confirmation whether Redwood allows a bridge letter if the report is older than 90 days.
2) Pen test: proposed window and whether Redwood requires staging access or if we can run an agent-based test. We also need the contact for scheduling and expected lead time.
3) Audit rights: scope (production vs. non-prod), notice period, and a proposed evidence cadence (what artifacts you can provide and how often).

Can you share a short matrix we can attach to the order form showing responsibilities (Redwood vs. ClearPath) and a suggested cadence for evidence delivery? Procurement needs those to finalize payment terms.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call early next week if that's easier.

—Alice

Alice — thanks for the clear list. See answers and an action ledger below; looping in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Contracts) for redline language and path to add the matrix to the Order Form / MSA. Monica (copied in next thread) will sync on pen-test ops.

Quick answers up front:
- SOC 2: latest report attached (SOC2-report-2027-Q2.pdf). We can provide a bridge letter for reports older than 90 days; provide the date you need covered and we'll produce it.
- Pen test: We support both agent-based and scheduled staging windows. Typical lead time is 4-6 weeks to schedule and verify controls. For production-facing tests we require a scoped change window and access control list; see pen-test-scope-clearpath.xlsx (attached).
- Audit rights / scope: Redwood proposes "limited audit rights" to require notice of 10 business days, a single auditor engaged by you (unless it's a regulator request), and production access limited to read-only logs and evidence collection unless we mutually agree to a wider scope in writing. Evidence cadence suggested below.

Action ledger (proposed):
- Redwood to deliver SOC 2 report + glossary of control mappings (by Sep 20) — Ben (done, attached).
- Redwood legal to propose MSA paragraph for audit rights and pen-test notification — Laura / Karthik (ETA 48 hrs).
- Redwood security to provide pen-test scheduling options and minimal test-runbook — Monica (ETA 3 business days).
- ClearPath to confirm preferred pen-test approach (agent vs. staging) and any vendor PO requirements — Alice (please advise).

Suggested evidence cadence (matrix to include on order form):
- SOC 2 report: on receipt (attachment) + annual thereafter.
- Pen-test results: summary report delivered within 10 business days after test completion; technical findings redacted for PII and narrow scope.
- Weekly token/latency cost reports: monthly (or as requested) — operational.
- On-demand audit evidence (e.g., logs, config snapshots): available within 5 business days for agreed categories; requests limited to once per quarter for non-regulatory audits.

Laura / Karthik — can you propose the specific MSA addendum: a short security exhibit + the order form matrix as an appendix. We're aiming to keep the exhibit one page and push detailed runbooks to a secure drive link.

Ben / Alice — high level redline suggested below for the MSA Security Exhibit. This is intentionally concise so the Order Form can surface the matrix and cadence. Happy to iterate.

Proposed MSA Security Exhibit language (draft):
"Security Exhibit — Audit and Testing
1. SOC 2: Redwood shall provide Customer with the latest SOC 2 Type II report upon execution of the Order Form. If the report is older than 90 days, Redwood will provide a bridge letter covering the requested period upon Customer request.
2. Penetration Testing: Customer may request a penetration test of Redwood services as described in the Order Form appendix. Redwood shall reasonably coordinate test windows. Production-facing tests are permitted only with prior written approval and a mutually agreed scope.
3. Audit Rights: Customer shall provide Redwood with at least ten (10) business days' notice prior to on-site or remote evidence collection. Evidence requests shall be limited to one (1) non-regulatory audit per quarter without Redwood's prior written consent. Sensitive operational runbooks and raw logs are Redwood internal documentation and will only be provided to Customer under a mutually agreed scope and appropriate NDAs.

- Recommend moving detailed scheduling/routing/runbooks to a shared secure folder and linking that in the Order Form appendix to avoid coupling detailed ops into the contractual exhibit.
- For pen-tests, we should include a short checklist (pre-test readiness, contact matrix, SLA for remediation acknowledgement) in the appendix.

Karthik — if that looks good, I suggest we prepare a redline MSA/Order Form and a two-column appendix (what Redwood provides vs. what Customer must do) for signature.

Alice — quick note on pen-test ops. We prefer a two-track approach:

Option A (staging window): Redwood provides staging environment and time-boxed access. This is the fastest route for full-stack tests and supports Burp/active scans. Typical timeline: schedule 4 weeks out, 48-hour test window, summary delivered within 10 business days.

Option B (agent-based): Customer installs a lightweight agent to run tests and return results to Redwood's secure upload. Minimal impact to prod; faster scheduling (2 weeks) but limited visibility on infra-level issues.

Pre-test checklist (we'll include in appendix):
- Scope doc (signed)
- Contact matrix with emergency on-call number
- Expected start/end times and rollback plan
- Data handling: no exfiltration, agreed redaction rules

Next steps: if ClearPath prefers staging, provide 3 preferred windows and we'll confirm availability. If agent-based, share the vendor/toolchain and we'll run an internal security review prior to approval.

Thanks — Monica
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
